reviews.title: Expensive

reviews.title: UPDATED Unable to scan multiple pages for single receipt entry
reviews.text: Great app to log your receipts but it does not support scanning multiple pages for a single receipt. Some of my receipts don’t show what the charges are for on the total page so I need to include a second or 3rd page for a receipt entry. After emailing the company for instruction, they said “yes you can, good luck” basically. When I emailed back twice more for more specific clarification they have neglected to respond. There may be better options/scanners out there, but I paid for a year upfront. I’ll be looking in to other options next year UPDATE I have now heard back from the development team and was informed of a way to log multiple pages. It requires a little more effort, which is not ideal, but it is a way to scan multiple images. I have recommended they add the ability to scan multiple pages for a single receipt entry and will try the workaround method they described to me in the meanwhile. If added, a multiple image scan for a single receipt would make this app top tier imo

reviews.title: Expected something different,..
reviews.text: Upon downloading this he app in a great rush to get caught up on my receipts. The app appeared to be getting into position to make the scan of the receipt with the green capture field. The field had to be initiated with h the take a picture button at the bottom of the screen, and the first capture was a picture of the receipt, background and everything. So I tried it again, I am thinking that I know how he green field will capture the receipt and bring the receipt into frame and I will have a digital copy of my actual receipt. The second go to as the same, wrinkles and unevenness. I guess I expected more of a scan of the receipt than just a snap shot or pic of the receipt, especially with the green capture field moving and searching for the edges and format of the receipt. The app is pretty simple to use and after the accepted scan the price is 8.99 per month. I would like a more clear and detailed look to the receipts for ease of detail information if needed.

reviews.title: Requires too much manual manipulation
reviews.text: I currently have credit and debit as my budget tracking app. This app exports expenses easily to credit and debit, but when I scan receipts I would say it only recognizes the correct date, total, merchant about 50 to 60% of the time. Some of the receipts it never gets correct no matter how many different ways I try to scan it. Consequently I have to manually edit many of the purchases which makes this app less efficient for me. Increasing the accuracy or helping the app to learn receipts from stores I frequent (CVS receipt seemed to confuse it) would make it a time saver. The other feature that would be helpful is to get the app to recognize which account (credit card and which one, cash, etc) was charged and include that in the information about the purchase. Currently this app seems only marginally more effective than manual entry to me so I did not purchase the subscription.

reviews.title: Ok for very basic basics
reviews.text: This app is alright for tracking expenses and capturing receipts and invoices and then running a report for tax purposes. You can categorize expenses by type per their limited list and can add notes for each receipt. You can scan receipts they the app or upload thru the camera photo function. The bad aspect of this app is once the expenses are added and reports built (By the way, you can only create 2 reports in the free version) there is no way to sort by category, amount , date, vendor, etc. it’s essentially a list of chronological receipts based on the date they were added. This makes it extremely difficult for verification of recurring expenses that may occur weekly or monthly to ensure you’ve captured everything. It’s basically a list you must mull thru and no way to search or sort. Not the best, but works for very basic capture and storing and A report. The paid unlocked version is way to expensive considering the clunky user interface.

reviews.title: It’s ok
reviews.text: First the good parts: Slick interface and it captures and crops receipts quickly. The bad: Needs a few clicks to get to scanning, which is frustrating; Lacks folder organization; On Home Depot receipts it never gets the date and merchant right. I mean come on, that’s home depot we are talking about. I have tried all the receipt apps, and really like the interface and scan quality of this one, but I have to go through hundreds of receipts and fixing the merchant name and date on each one is not much better than manually scanning everything. Every other scanning app gets the Home Depot receipts right, but they are either not cropping the receipts or the quality is blurry. I hope this review helps the developers to improve on this app.

reviews.title: Potential for Greatness
reviews.text: I love this app. The functionality is great and it’s easy enough to add expenses. However, the app has lots of bugs. I am frequently booted out of my account and have to restore my subscription and sometimes I am unable to view my expenses or edit reports which can be really frustrating. Only use this if you have patience for a developing app with lots of bugs.

reviews.title: Too many bugs and lacks features
reviews.text: • can’t delete receipts or reports • the date after you scan a receipt is always one day prior to the date on the receipt so you have to manually change it • can’t search expenses by the month, date, category, or total amount only by the name • the reports have the wrong dates (this time, one day after the saved date) • the data is accessible even after you sign out • you can save future dates in expenses (like if you have a receipt from the future) The concept is great and has potential, but it needs to be better quality. Currently it looks like an app some kid made for a school project. There are much better apps out there for managing finances.
